title: Dimension Shield
text: “So then, shall we do Éclair-san next?”
“Ah, me? Is it truly permissible for someone like me to spar with you?”
“Sure thing! No need to be so formal about it.”
“Oh, Ren-kun. That cat over there gets awfully soft on serious, upstanding types, so watch out or she might just snatch him away, indeed.”
Ho-kun chimed in with some teasing.
“An NTR situation, I say! Ren already has Assistant, though. She’s the fickle sort, so it should be fine, I say!”
“Wh-what are you two even talking about!”
Ren protested to us, his face turning bright red. How amusing, indeed!

“Would you kindly not lump me in with that love-crazed bird? Well, I’ll admit I do have a soft spot for earnest sorts. That representative from the girls’ side in that peeping incident we talked about earlier was quite the serious type too.”
“I have no intention of pursuing romance in the first place, though.”
“Oh dear, sounds like the kind of line someone says right before missing their chance at marriage and losing some fight somewhere, ending up saying ‘kukuru’ in defeat.”
Ho-kun occasionally comes out with these otaku-flavored jokes that sound exactly like something Father would say when he’s in a teasing mood, indeed.
“So, Éclair-san. About what level of skill are you looking to train at? Something on par with Ren-kun?”
“I have already seen more than enough of your skill firsthand. I would prefer instruction in some original forms, if you would.”
“I see, I see. So you’re the type who takes an interest in forms.”
And so, while chatting away like this, Arc and the others seemed to be exchanging all sorts of information during the morning training session, indeed.

Having witnessed that exchange of information, I went to consult with Doctor and the others about Filolial-sama’s health, only to find Arc, Ho-kun, Father, Big Sister, and Raph-chan all gathered in the research lab, apparently deep in conversation about something. Since I was already there, I figured I’d join the circle and listen in, indeed. Doctor kept nodding along vigorously as she listened to Arc.
“So you do it like this, and then like this—now let’s prepare the bullets—”
“Dusting off old skills again, are we? Making strange weapons during an alchemy lecture, I see.”
“What’s wrong with that? It’s a demonstration! There, all done—Composite Magic Bullet Gun: Elemental Bullet, complete with a full set of ammunition.”
“…That looks like a weapon that could summon monsters or something.”
Arc had been clattering away, assembling parts to build a gun, indeed.

“If we gave this to Itsuki Kawasumi-kun, the Bow Hero, I think he’d gain quite a bit of combat power. You can choose elements freely, and in this world… I’d wager you could even cast spells that normally require multiple people to activate, don’t you think?”
“Sounds like a fairly powerful weapon.”

“Yep.” With that, Arc handed the gun to Doctor, the one person present unbound by any hero’s restrictions, indeed. Doctor struck a pose as if test-firing it, and when she pulled the trigger, flames burst forth from the gun. Then, loading multiple rounds with a click and pulling the trigger again, clouds formed inside the room and lightning crackled forth.
“The test rounds were kept extremely small, but if you use these other bullets, you could crank up the power considerably.”
“Alchemy from another world truly is amazing. There’s an endless amount of technology I don’t know about—it’s quite educational.”

Apparently, Doctor had stopped speaking human language for a time due to her fieldwork days, but after Father assigned her to work in the village, she reportedly regained her ability to speak with people. She could communicate perfectly fine with Filolial-sama and Filo-tan without any issue, indeed. Incidentally, Assistant had also gone through a phase of laughing strangely. According to Father, both Doctor and Assistant tend to go a bit odd if they spend too much time living among monster habitats, so they need to be kept in human settlements in moderation.
“This is technology that existed in this world long ago, you know. Thanks to some troublemaker who caused problems around here, it seems there was a significant break in technological continuity.”
“Sounds about right. Even the Queen seemed to vaguely sense something along those lines.”
“Well, if civilization advances too much, that brings its own set of problems, so it’s a double-edged sword either way.”
Arc murmured this with a sigh, indeed. Somehow, I sensed in those words the weight of hard-won experience—the kind of thing only someone who’d truly lived through it could say.
“All we can do is make sure it gets passed down as a cautionary tale for later generations.”
“I think you’ll be just fine. Anthreya, huh—that’s a surname I’ve actually encountered before, back when I came to this world long ago.”
“Sounds like you’re saying you met one of my ancestors.”

“I did meet her. And I don’t mean some past-life knowledge nonsense—she was, quite literally, a genuine prodigy who developed technology leagues beyond what the rest of the world’s civilization had achieved.”
I hope you can surpass that ancestor of yours someday. Arc said this with a smile, indeed.
“My ancestor… I wonder what kind of person she was? Unfortunately, my family’s full of engineering types, and with so many relatives, I can’t really keep track of them all.”
“She hated dragons, that one.”
“Hating dragons, generation after generation, huh… Maybe that streak of yours is just some ancestral throwback.”
Father gave Doctor a faint smile.
“Who knows, really. Oh, by the way, she became the Whip Hero. Now that I look closely, the resemblance is there. No doubt about it—she’s definitely your ancestor.”
“There are occasional records in family lineages about someone becoming a hero, but the truth of it is always murky. Still, if a living witness to history vouches for it, I suppose that settles it.”
“You practically forced this thing on me. You should be the one taking it up now, honestly.”
Assistant tried shoving the whip onto Doctor, but Doctor simply ignored her, clearly wanting nothing to do with it.
“So what kind of person was she, exactly?”

“She took issue with the idea that dragons stood at the top of the monster hierarchy and researched ways to challenge that. She strengthened the balloon-type monsters in this world to rival dragons in power, and made all sorts of other modifications to the monsters here too.”
“You’ve said something pretty similar yourself, haven’t you.”
“Raph.”
Doctor had been researching the Raph-species that Father created back when he was in good health, indeed.
“Specifically, what kind of modifications did she make?”
“Seems she did a lot of different things, but from what I gather, she made it so corrupted souls couldn’t enter a monster’s body.”
“…So in this world, it’s simply impossible for a reincarnator’s soul to be reborn as a monster?”
“If the soul isn’t corrupted, I think it’s possible. There are various complicated conditions—like originally being from this world and so on.”
“Raph.”
Big Sister picked Raph-chan up and lifted her up and down. Father watched the two of them with a warm, gentle smile. Ho-kun turned his gaze toward them as well.
“Feeling a bit lonely, being left out of the conversation, Ho-kun?”
“No, not really… that’s not it at all, is it?”
“No need to hold back, indeed. What are you good at, Ho-kun? I’d love for you to teach me, I say.”
“Being fussed over like that just makes it worse, honestly—please stop.”
“That bird over there is skilled with magical script. In this world, I suppose that would be the hero’s script.”
Ah, the sort of thing readable on Cal Mira Island or in records left behind by heroes, indeed.
“So it’s just being able to write characters?”
“No, not quite. Master it properly, and you could even nullify that defensive membrane the mastermind behind the world fusion incident deployed—the one they call the Dimension Shield.”

Ho-kun explained this so casually, indeed. That was the thing with the strange resistance I’d felt when attacking the Crimson Swine’s main body. It had felt like a solid shield, yet the sensation upon striking it had been decidedly odd.
“That’s quite the sudden technical term… but is that the thing Spear 0 managed to pierce through?”
Ho-kun let out a sigh at Father’s question.

“Hah… that method wasn’t exactly the proper way to deal with it. What that does is forcibly nullify something that the world itself hasn’t sanctioned—it’s the equivalent of, say, dealing with a virus-infected computer in your world by just doing a clean install. Crude, and far from the correct approach.”
“So how do you break through it properly, then?”
“I suppose it’s better to first understand the structure of the Dimension Shield itself, don’t you think?”
Overcoming with the correct method what had previously only been forced open through Spear 0. As expected of Ho-kun. Truly the most knowledgeable of Filolial-sama, indeed!
“I see…”

“That said, the mechanism itself is really just an application of spatial displacement combined with point-targeted sniping. It shifts the space around the person, redirecting any incoming attack into another dimension entirely—and it’s set up to be one-way, with no reciprocal effect possible. Essentially, it’s a barrier that allows one-sided interference only.”

Somehow, I felt like I’d gotten a rough grasp of the mechanism, indeed. In other words, the moment an attack made contact, a teleportation skill would shunt it off to some other location—or rather, redirect the trajectory of the attack elsewhere. It reminded me of the Mirror Vassal Weapon Kou possesses, which has a skill that redirects attacks through a mirror.
